primary_question: Why don't Blinkit users explore new categories?

notes: Behavioral clusters observed: {'Price Sensitive': 1736, 'Routine Buyers': 554, 'Explorers': 348, 'Impulse Buyers': 180}

Top themes: good good / good / sarvice good / good sarvice, 3स / 3स 𝙜𝙤𝙤𝙙 / 5star / 5star ooo, hai / bhi / bahut / nahi, nice nice / nice / good nice / nice good, good service / fast service / service good / service fast

executive_summary: Across 3,200 multi-source reviews (852 exploration-relevant), users mostly stay in grocery routines or bounce when discovery, quality trust, or price clarity fail. Dominant barriers: dont trust quality for new category, price uncertainty new category, coverage or eta. Category expansion opportunity concentrates in snacks, home, electronics. Recommended next step: run discovery-rail + first-buy guarantee experiments on the top blocked categories.

jobs_to_be_done.job: When I need something outside my usual grocery list, I want to trust the assortment and quality so I can order without second-guessing.
jobs_to_be_done.situation: Expanding beyond staples into beauty, electronics, home, or pet
jobs_to_be_done.desired_outcome: Confidence that the category is as reliable as grocery
jobs_to_be_done.current_workaround: Order only staples on Blinkit; buy elsewhere for other categories

jobs_to_be_done.job: When I'm browsing under time pressure, I want new categories to surface in context so I don't have to know what to search.
jobs_to_be_done.desired_outcome: Serendipitous but relevant discovery without leaving the flow
jobs_to_be_done.current_workaround: Stay on the same SKUs / search only known brands

jobs_to_be_done.job: When trying a new category for the first time, I want clear price and return signals so the risk feels bounded.
jobs_to_be_done.situation: First purchase in electronics / beauty / pharmacy-adjacent
jobs_to_be_done.desired_outcome: Transparent fees, quality cues, easy undo
jobs_to_be_done.current_workaround: Abandon cart or stick to grocery where risk is known

unmet_needs.need: Visible, trusted paths into non-grocery categories during habitual grocery sessions
unmet_needs.pain: Discovery is search-dependent; reorderers never see adjacency

unmet_needs.need: Risk reducers (returns, authenticity, freshness) for first buys outside grocery
unmet_needs.pain: Quality distrust blocks trial even when assortment exists

unmet_needs.need: All-in price clarity before commitment on unfamiliar categories
Assortment confidence signals (in stock, alternatives) for expansion categories
unmet_needs.pain: Empty or sparse shelves teach users 'Blinkit isn't for this'

hypotheses.statement: Users fail to explore new categories because in-app discovery does not surface adjacent categories during grocery sessions.
Users avoid new categories because quality/authenticity risk feels higher than grocery.
Users hesitate on new categories when all-in price and fees are unclear relative to offline.
Power users stay in reorder loops that never expose non-grocery demand.
Exploration intent dies when expected SKUs are missing or out of stock.
ETA/coverage anxiety reduces willingness to try unfamiliar categories.

testable_experiments.name: Category discovery rail after grocery add
testable_experiments.intervention: After adding a staple, show a contextual 'also useful tonight' rail from an adjacent category with trust badges.
testable_experiments.primary_metric: Attach rate of non-grocery SKU in same session
testable_experiments.guardrail: Checkout completion rate must not drop >2%
testable_experiments.sample_size_note: Power for 15% relative lift in attach; ~2 weeks on high-traffic cities

testable_experiments.name: First-buy quality guarantee for new categories
testable_experiments.intervention: Offer one-tap easy return + quality score for first purchase in beauty/electronics/home.
testable_experiments.primary_metric: First-time category conversion among grocery-only cohorts
testable_experiments.sample_size_note: Stratify by city tier; exclude surge-heavy hours

testable_experiments.name: Upfront fee clarity on new-category PDPs
testable_experiments.intervention: Show all-in price (item + fees) and 'vs offline' cue on first-time category PDPs.
testable_experiments.guardrail: No increase in support tickets tagged 'hidden fees'

testable_experiments.name: Routine break prompt for power reorderers
testable_experiments.intervention: For users with 5+ identical reorder carts, surface one curated 'try something new' pack with free delivery on first try.
testable_experiments.primary_metric: Share of sessions with ≥1 new category SKU

category_opportunities.why_now: Adjacent to grocery — easiest expansion wedge.
Assortment gaps and 'not for Blinkit' mental model.
High intent + high distrust; quality and authenticity cues matter most.
Niche but sticky once tried; trust on freshness/expiry.
Discovery-friendly but needs sampling / return confidence.
